current_activity: II Parachute Corps diversionary feint north from St. Lô along the east bank of the Vire
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7 p. 137: the II Parachute Corps was to launch a feint directly north from St. Lô in a limited objective attack along the east bank of the Vire River in support of the 11 July Panzer Lehr attack; the jump-off was scheduled for 0145, 11 July. Location: St. Lô sector, the start of the feint. Location approximate: the source names St. Lô and the east bank of the Vire; no corps command post. Event support: the source states the planned feint and its jump-off time; the Green Book does not report its result in the text read. Commander: General der Fallschirmtruppen Eugen Meindl (ch. 2 p. 29, in mid-June).

location_qualifier: between Magny and St. Lambert; crossing area
current_activity: II Parachute Corps breakout column reaches the Dives between Magny and St. Lambert about 0030
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 542-543: the forward elements left la Londe at 2230 on 19 August; the paratroopers reached the Dives around 0030 on 20 August somewhere between Magny and St. Lambert, and Meindl crossed the river about half a mile downstream from St. Lambert. Location: between Magny and St. Lambert, the source place of the first crossing attempt; the point is St. Lambert. Location approximate: Magny is not in the place list. Commander: General der Fallschirmtruppen Eugen Meindl (ch. 27 p. 538, 543). Context: Hausser broke out with the paratroopers; the corps then headed for Mt. Ormel near Coudehard.

notes: Event date: CMH Siegfried Line Campaign ch. 8 p. 193: "Despite the reinforcement of Corps Feldt by seven battalions under the II Parachute Corps, the Germans had been thrown on the defensive in this sector"; Model assigned the First Parachute Army "General Meindl's II Parachute Corps". Location approximate: a sector point; the corps headquarters is not placed. Location support: CMH puts the corps and Corps Feldt in the Nijmegen sector. Commander: General Meindl. Opponents: US 82nd Airborne Division.

notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 14 p. 314: "the condition of the II Parachute Corps at nightfall on 24 March actually was precarious"; "General Meindl would have no choice but to pull back the paratroopers forming his left wing along the Rhine and face them to the east".
